6487.t: CE6472: Remote Sensing and GIS Laboratory
6487.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6472 : Remote Sensing and GIS Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I [6hrs]
1. To geo-reference a given map using Arc-GIS software.
2. To extract the region of interest (ROI) from the selected study area and to create slope and contour map.
Module II [6hrs]
1. To fill the DEM, create a flow accumulation map, and generate flow direction, stream order, and stream-to-feature maps
2. To develop a workflow for processing Landsat-8 data, creating composite bands, mosaicking multiple tiles, and extracting ROIs.
Module III [9hrs]
1. To classify the land use and cover using iso-cluster unsupervised classification method.
2. To classify the land use and cover of an area using the maximum likelihood supervised classification method.
3. To assess the accuracy of the supervised classification method through kappa co-efficient.
Module IV [9hrs]
1. To derive the vegetation index, normalized difference vegetation index, normalized difference water index, and normalized difference built-up index of a region to characterize the status and variability of vegetation, soil, water, and landscape.
2. To determine the land surface temperature of a specified region by analyzing various factors, including spectral radiance, atmospheric brightness temperature, normalized difference vegetation index, the proportion of vegetation, and land surface emissivity.
3. To produce a spatial distribution map showing the variation of rainfall by utilizing the IDW technique.

Course Objective

1 .

To make the students familiar with remote sensing technology and its uses.
2 .

To equip the students with map development capabilities
3 .

To provide adequate exposure to the students to the state of the art software used for image processing
4 .

To enable students to use the gained knowledge for water resources management

Course Outcome

1 .

On completion of the course, the student should be capable
CO1: To acquire knowledge about digital image processing techniques
CO2: To prepare classified maps employing supervised and unsupervised classification algorithms
CO3: To enable students to manage spatial data in digital format
CO4: To prepare thematic maps using GIS
CO5: To understand the use of remote sensing and GIS for solving problems related to water resources

Essential Reading

1 .

Manual of ArcGIS, Manual of ERDAS IMAGINE, ESRI

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Lavender, S., and Lavender, A., Practical Handbook of Remote Sensing, CRC Press

2 .

Jenson, J., Remote Sensing of the Environment: An Earth Resource Perspective, Prentice Hall

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH3007 : Electricity and Magnetism { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: (6 hours)
Vector Analysis: Vector Algebra, Differential Calculus, Integral Calculus, Curvilinear Coordinates, The Dirac Delta Function.
Module 2: (8 hours)
Electrostatics: Electric Field, Divergence and Curl of Electrostatic Fields, Electric Potential, Work and Energy in Electrostatics, Conductors.
Module 3: (8 hours)
Potentials: Laplace’s Equation, The Method of Images, Separation of Variables, Multipole Expansion.
Module 4: (8 hours)
Magnetostatics: The Lorentz Force Law, The Biot-Savart Law, The Divergence and Curl of B, Magnetic Vector Potential.
Module 5: (6 hours)
Electrodynamics: Electromotive Force, Electromagnetic Induction, Electric and Magnetic Fields in Matter, Maxwell’s Equations.

Course Objective

1 .

1. To learn the basic mathematical tools required for the understanding of this course.
2 .

2. Electric field due to a charged body and calculating its electric potential, work done, etc.
3 .

3. Laplace equation and method of images, to calculate potential and its higher order terms.
4 .

4. Magnetic field due to steady current flow and its vector potential.
5. Electric and magnetic field inside matter and corresponding Maxwell’s equation.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students will be able to:
CO1: Learn the basic mathematical tools required for this course.
CO2: Find the electric field and its curl and divergence due to charged objects.
CO3: Calculate the potential due to a charged object and its multipole expansion.
CO4: Find the magnetic field and its curl and divergence due to steady current flow.
CO5: Calculate electric field, magnetic field, and Maxwell’s equation for vacuum and matter.

D. J. Griffiths, Introduction to electrodynamics, Prentice Hall , 4th Edition (2025).

2 .

E. M. Purcell and D.J. Morin, Electricity and Magnetism, Cambridge University Press , 2013

Supplementary Reading

2 .

John David Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics, Wiley and sons Ltd. , 3rd Edition

5975.t: CY4704: Mathematical and Computational Methods in Chemistry
5975.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CY4704 : Mathematical and Computational Methods in Chemistry { 1-0-2 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Mathematics for chemistry: Fundamental theorem of calculus, series and limits, Euler’s formula, ODEs, Fourier transforms, operators, functions of several variables, matrix eigenvalue problem, vector space, probability, correlations. Basic understanding of computational chemistry, use of Linux operating system.
Numerical computing using scientific language: Elements of Fortran programming, constants, variables and operators, control statements, I/O operations, functions, loops, DATA statements, arrays, sub programs, DATA files. Roots of equations, truncation and round off errors, interpolation, differentiation and integration, linear equations, matrix operations, regression analysis and least square fit.
Applications to chemistry: statistical thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, calculation of energies associated to molecular systems, curve fitting. Use of software packages: visualization and plotting, semi-empirical methods.

Course Objective

1 .

This course will explain different mathematical methods and the direct use of numerical methods in chemistry and compare those results with the available experimental data.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: It will help students to solve chemical problems using mathematical and computational techniques
CO2: Basic guidance of quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations
CO3: Apply computational chemistry techniques to the problems in various fields like drug discovery, materials science, and environmental chemistry

19799.t: MN4103: Computerized Mine Planning and Design
19799.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MN4103 : Computerized Mine Planning and Design { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction: Mine planning and its importance; Components of mine planning, Technical and economic considerations for planning, Engineering studies (PFS, FS, DFS), Introduction to resource estimation approaches
Preparation of feasibility report and detailed project report. Production planning and scheduling. Examples of Mine Planning Report in India and abroad
Module 2 :

Planning and Design of Surface Mine: Geometrical considerations for design of surface mines: Pit geometry, Pit layouts – Mine access, pit expansion and push back operation.
Pit Planning and Design: Pit design, Cut-off grade and its estimation; Compositing, Ultimate pit design – hand method, floating cone technique, Lerchs-Grossmann (LG) algorithm. Optimum mine size and Taylor’s mine life rule, Lane’s Algrithm. Production Scheduling-Concepts
Module 3 :

Underground Mine Planning: Mining method selection, Stope planning: Selection of stopping methods, Evaluate stope dimension. Design of remnant pillars (crown/sill pillar). Production planning: Stope reserve, development, manpower, ore/waste handling, essential services, production scheduling, Optimization of mine size (mine production capacity) based on techno-economic considerations;

Module 4 :

Equipment and Infrastructure planning: Equipment system selection –for surface mines and underground mines. Mine infrastructure planning- optimal location of mine entries, associated mine infrastructure (plant, workshop, statutory buildings, layout) and its significance

Module 5 :

Mine closure planning: Initial, Progressive and Final Mine Closure Planning and its components; Legal and Financial Aspects. Rehabilitation, mine closure and post-industrial land use planning.
Module 6 :

Introduction, Uses, Examples of industry standard software and use cases. Digitalization and Automation in Mines, Use of drones and Lidar in mining. Ore loss and dilutions/Grade Control in Mines, Mine to Mill Reconciliation. Technical Auditing and Benchmarking
Case studies on various aspects planning and designing of coal and metal mines through opencast and underground mining methods

Course Objective

1 .

To create awareness on various features of mine planning as compared to other industries

2 .

Provide information on preparation of feasibility report and detailed project report with reference to Indian mining requirements
3 .

To help students in planning mines for required production, productivity, etc. for underground and opencast mines

4 .

To understand various tools and software used for planning, design and operation of mines

Course Outcome

1 .

Understand various concepts of Mining methods and required techno-economic studies
2 .

Impart knowledge of basic & advanced principles of surface mine planning for development and extraction of minerals
3 .

Ability to plan and design underground metalliferous mines considering the statutory and techno-economic requirements
4 .

Understand mine equipment selection and infrastructure planning
5 .

Comprehend the nature, type and necessity of mine closure planning
6 .

To understand various tools and software used for planning, design and operation of mines
